name: meertrack API
description:
Machine-readable contract for the meertrack v1 API. Use it to
generate clients, import into Postman/Stoplight, or validate requests
and responses.

Auth: every request must include `Authorization: Bearer mt_live_…`.
Keys are minted in the app at Settings → API Keys (admin only).

Rate limit: 60 requests per minute, per workspace, **per serverless
instance**. The limiter is in-process - there is no shared Redis. In
practice this means:
- The `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header reflects the counter on the
  instance that served the current request only. Successive requests
  may be routed to different instances, so the value is not monotonic.
- A burst across multiple cold instances can briefly exceed 60 rpm in
  aggregate. Don't design clients that rely on exactly-60 enforcement.
- Treat 429 + `X-RateLimit-Reset` as the authoritative backoff signal
  and apply jitter; do not extrapolate from `X-RateLimit-Remaining`.

Every successful response and every rate-limited response carries the
`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`
headers. 401 responses carry `WWW-Authenticate` instead.

Parameter validation is strict. On the filtering endpoints
(`/competitors`, `/activity`, `/activity/items`, `/digests`) an
unrecognized query parameter returns `400 unknown_parameter` naming
the offending parameter, and an out-of-range value returns
`400 invalid_parameter` - neither is ignored. Comma-separated
parameters may also be repeated (`?id=A&id=B` is equivalent to
`?id=A,B`); repeating a non-list parameter is an error.

Versioning & deprecation: this is `v1`. Backwards-incompatible
changes ship as `v2` at a new path prefix; `v1` will continue to be
served. One exception, effective 1.1.0: the strict parameter
validation described above was introduced on `v1` rather than held
for `v2`, because the previous behavior returned `200` with
unfiltered data for a request the server had not understood - a
silently wrong answer we judged worse than a breaking change.
Field-level deprecations are announced on a deprecated field via an
`x-deprecated` extension and a `Deprecation: true` header on
affected responses, with at least 90 days' notice before removal;
deprecated *parameters* are marked `deprecated: true` in this
document and echoed in an `X-Meertrack-Deprecated-Parameter`
response header. Subscribe to changes by watching the `info.version`
field in this document - the patch version bumps for additive
changes, the minor version for backwards-compatible behavior
changes.

Questions or access requests: [contact us](https://meertrack.com/contact).
